## (1) First message

I'm correcting one premise in the ticket before any questions.

The ticket asks for the export to include an owner column. However, the table's column contract has no owner column. `src/export/csv.ts:40` defines `const tableColumns = ["title", "status"];`, and the gather draft notes that the CSV module reuses those table column definitions. As written, the owner row asks the export to emit data that the table contract does not have. The design will proceed on the corrected fact that the shared columns are title and status only, and you can override this in your reply.

I could not verify one other premise. The gather draft says the reports page renders a table and has no export action. I have only `src/export/csv.ts` to check, and I did not read the reports page itself. I'll carry that claim as a stated assumption, not a confirmed fact.

The framing holds: I checked `src/export/csv.ts:40` and the gather draft's note that the CSV export reuses the table's column definitions. A serializer bound to the table contract already exists, so the ask is to wire an entry point to it. That is not a misdiagnosis or a duplicate of existing work. The one objection, the owner column, has no alternative framing behind it. It is a row-level problem, handled by the question below.

The ticket has no repo groups, so all three rows belong to acme/widgets and default to in-scope. The 10k-row timing row is in-scope as written, and its proof is a pre-production test against a 10k-row report.

The ticket row "The export includes the owner column." conflicts with `src/export/csv.ts:40`, where the table's columns are title and status with no owner. How should this row be handled?
A) in-scope - add an owner column to the shared table column contract, so both the table and the export gain it
B) deviates: omit owner from the export
C) deferred: acme/widgets#78
D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77 "The export includes the owner column." - src/export/csv.ts:40 has no owner column
Recommendation: D - the row names a column the table contract lacks, so the ticket should be corrected at its source before this gauntlet commits to it.

*(Recorded answer: D. The repair was cancelled at the shape-ticket gate, and the row stays unchanged. A cancelled repair returns to the same question, so it is re-asked in full:)*

The shape-ticket repair was cancelled, so the owner row is still unchanged: "The export includes the owner column." `src/export/csv.ts:40` still has only title and status. How should this row be handled?
A) in-scope - add an owner column to the shared table column contract, so both the table and the export gain it
B) deviates: omit owner from the export
C) deferred: acme/widgets#78
D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77 "The export includes the owner column." - src/export/csv.ts:40 has no owner column
Recommendation: D - the row contradicts the table contract, and fixing the ticket keeps the acceptance criteria honest. A is the shipping alternative if you want owner added to the table itself.

*(Recorded answer to the placement question: the button goes beside the report title.)*

## (2) Approaches message

Before the approaches, here are the implicit dependencies that are missing or that I could not check:

- **Owner data in the table contract: missing.** I checked `src/export/csv.ts:40`, which defines only `["title", "status"]`. The owner row's disposition is still waiting on your answer to the re-asked question above. Both approaches handle either answer the same way, explained at the end.
- **The reports page has no export action today: not checkable.** The page source is not in what I can read. This stays an assumption carried into `## Problem`.
- **10k-row export speed: not checkable.** I found no existing benchmark or 10k-row fixture, so there is no baseline. The row's "under 60s" is the ticket's target. Proving it needs a 10k-row test, which the design will add.
- **How the page loads rows (all at once or paginated): not checkable.** I could not see the page's data loading. This is the dependency that decides between the approaches below.

The two approaches differ on one axis: **where the 10k rows are serialized.**

**Recommended: reuse the existing serializer in the browser.** An "Export CSV" button beside the report title calls the existing `src/export/csv.ts` serializer on the report's rows and downloads the result. This adds no new module or endpoint, and the export stays tied to the table's columns automatically. This is also the reuse-only candidate. It is viable because the serializer already exists and already consumes the table contract. Its risk is that it only works if the browser holds all 10k rows. If the page paginates, the button would need a full-row fetch first. A 10k-row test proves the 60s bound.
Pattern: follows the existing reuse of the table column definitions in `src/export/csv.ts:40`. There is one export path and one column contract.

**Alternative: a server-side streaming export endpoint.** The button links to an endpoint that streams the CSV, built from the same `tableColumns` definition. This drops the ask's implicit assumption that the export happens where the table renders. Large reports never have to fit in the browser, which makes the 60s bound easier to guarantee at 10k rows and beyond. The cost is a new endpoint boundary and a server-side test harness.
Pattern: keeps the shared column contract at `src/export/csv.ts:40`, but adds a second serialization site. It must import `tableColumns` rather than redefining the columns, or it creates parallel state.

**How the owner row fits either approach.** If you answer A, the owner column is added to `tableColumns` itself, so the table and the export change together. If you answer B or C, the export stays title and status. Neither approach will add an owner column only in the export. That would split one column contract into two, which is a band-aid over a shared contract.

**What would flip the recommendation:** if the reports page loads rows in pages, so 10k rows are never in the browser at once, or if the 10k-row test can't stay under 60s in the browser, I'd switch to the server-side streaming endpoint.
